The Petitioner has filed this petition under Sec.166 of Indian Motor Vehicles Act seeking compensation of Rs.5,50,000/- for the damages suffered to the Petitioner's Car in a road accident dated 29.09.2023.
It is to be noted here that, as per the documents the accident date was 09.09.2023 but its wrongly typed in the plaint as 29.09.2023 instead of 09.09.2023.
Hence, the accident 09.09.2023 is taken into consideration.

2. The case of the Petitioner in brief is as follows:-
That on 09.09.2023 at about 09.00pm the petitioner was driving his Maruthi Suzuki - ALTO - k10, Black VXI vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-41-P-2580 on NH-48 from Bengaluru - Tumkur NH-48 Road, Kengal Kempohalli, Near Govt. School,
Nelamangala, while so proceeding a Cement Bulkar Bharat Benz bearing vehicle Reg.No.KA-01- AE-5124 Lorry came at high speed, in a rash and negligent manner,
without following any traffic rules, tried to overtake the petitioner's Car and hit two doors on the right side of the Car by overtaking the said car came from right side to immediate left and pulled/dragged the said Car for more than 100 meters even without the knowledge that he is dragging the said Car in a rash and negligent manner by endangering human life.
Due to impact, the petitioner's Maruthi Suzuki Alto - Kio, Black VXI vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-41-P-2580 two doors on the right side of the Car was heavily damaged.

Immediately after the accident, the petitioner took his car to the Service Station for repairs and tinkering at Kalyani Motors (P)
Ltd., due to heavy damages it takes around 21 days to complete the services of the Car.
Accordingly, on 30.09.2023, the petitioner took delivery of the Car and totally spend Rs.67,940/- incurred for damages and service expenses of the Car.
3. It is the further case of the petitioner that, the accident is solely due to the rash and negligent driving of the Cement Bulkar Bharat Benz bearing vehicle Reg.NO.KA- 01-AE-5124.
Prior to the date of accident, the petitioner's car was in good condition.

On account of the said accident, the Udaya Shankar S vs Gopi Y on 4 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/17278915/
2 petitioner cannot attend his work for so many days, resulting in loss of earning and usage of Car and put him a great financial hardship.

sentences.text: The Nelamangala Traffic Police have registered case against the driver of the offending Cement Bulkar Bharat Benz bearing No.KA-01-AE-5124 in Cr.No.0385/2023 p/u/Sec.279 of the IPC.
Therefore, the respondents being the Driver, owner and insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
4. In spite of due service of notice, the respondent Nos.1 & 2 did not appear hence, placed ex-parte.
In response to the notice issued by this Tribunal, the respondent No.3 appeared and filed written statement.

5. The written statement of the respondent No.3 is as follows:
It has denied all the petition averments except admitting the issuance of policy to the Goods Carrier bearing No.KA-01-AE-5124 in favour of the Respondent No.1 and the policy was in force (from 09.07.2023 to 08.07.2024) as on the date of accident.
Further submitted that, as per Sec.II-I(ii) of the policy, the liability in respect of third party property damage is limited to Rs.7,50,000/-only.
Further stated that, the petitioner was driving his car without having a valid DL.
It has denied the involvement of the offending vehicle in the accident.
Further, the Insured i.e., 1st respondent has knowingly entrusted the insured vehicle to the driver, who had no valid and effective driving license.
There is no compliance of Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of MV Act.
Further contended that the accident occurred sole negligence on the part of the petitioner himself.
There is no negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.

Further denied the vehicle damage repair expenses, manner of accident, damages to the vehicle etc., Further contended that the compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly excessive and prayed for dismissal of the petition.
6.

On the above rival contentions of the parties, this court has framed the following Issues:-
1.

Whether the petitioner proves that, the accident occurred on 29-09-2023 at 03.00pm due to rash and negligent driving of driver of Cement Bulkar Bharat Benz bearing Reg.No.KA-01- AE-5124 and in the said accident petitioner's Maruthi Alto K10 car bearing Reg.No.KA-41-P-2580 sustained damages?
2. Whether the Petitioner is entitled for Compensation?
If so, what is the quantum?

From whom?
3.
What order or award?
7. The Petitioner in order to prove his case, has examined himself as PW.1 and got marked 18 documents as per Exs.P.1 to P.18.
On the other side the Respondent No.3 has got examined its official as RW.1 and got marked Ex.R.1.

sentences.text: Heard the arguments of the learned counsel for both the parties and perused the materials on record.
The learned counsel for the Respondent No.3 has submitted the written arguments.

9. On hearing both sides and perusal of the evidence on records this court answers the above issues as follows:-
 Issue No.1: In the affirmative  Issue No.2: Partly In the affirmative.

Issue No.3: As per the final order,
 for the following:-
 REASONS

10. Issue No.1:
The Petitioner to prove that the accident occurred due to actionable negligence of the part of the driver of the offending Cement Bulkar Bharat Benz has examined himself as PW.1 and produced 18 documents as per Exs.P.1 to P.18.
He has reiterated the contents of the petition in his affidavit filed in lieu of his chief examination.

He has also produced documents such as FIR in Cr. No.0385/2023 of Nelmangala Traffic Police with complaint, charge sheet, PF Form, spot mahazar, policy notice and reply and IMV report as per Exs.P.1 to P.5 & 18.
All these documents are public documents which have got presumptive value under law.
The respondent No.3 has denied the rash and negligent driving by the driver of the offending Cement Bulkar bearing No.KA-01-AE-5124 and also denied the case of the petitioner.
In this regard the respondent No.3 has got examined RW.1 and got marked Ex.R.1.
In the cross-examination of PW.1, he has deposed that the car belongs to him only.
He was proceeding from Bangalore towards Tumakuru in the National Highway.
He was driving the said Car.
Further admitted that the traffic is heavy in the National Highway.
Cement Bulker was coming behind his Car and he observed it.
It was about 20-25ft away behind the Car.
He only gave complaint.

He also denied other suggestions made by the counsel for R-3.
11.

On perusal of Ex.P.1/FIR with complaint and Charge sheet at Ex.P.2 it is clearly mentioned that the petitioner was owner of the Maruthi Alto K-10 Car bearing Reg.No.KA-41-P-25803 and in police documents nothing is found to show that the petitioner was not the owner of the said car as on the date of accident.

The charge sheet is filed against the driver of the offending Cement Bulkar, which was not challenged by the said owner and no contrary evidence is forthcoming to prove that there was negligence on the part of the petitioner's driver and there was no negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle.
As such, there are no reasons to discard and disbelieve the version of Petitioner and documents produced before this court.
Ex.P.2 charge sheet shows that, the charge sheet was filed against the driver of the offending vehicle holding that he was driving the vehicle in a rash and negligent manner and caused the accident.
It is undisputed fact that the First Information report is clearly revels that the complaint has been lodged on the same day of incident.

4 Information Statement indicates that the complaint has lodged on 09.09.2023 at about 05.00hours against to accident occurred on 09.09.2023 at about 03:00 Hours.

sentences.text: It is well settled position of law that the proceedings under Motor Vehicle Act are summary in nature and it is beneficial legislation and the evidence required about negligence act is sufficient if it is in the nature of preponderance of probability.

Under these circumstances, relying upon the oral evidence of PW.1 coupled with the documents produced as per Exs.P.1 to P.5 & 18, this Tribunal is of view that the accident has occurred due to the rash and negligent driving by the driver of the offending Cement Bulkar bearing No.KA- 01-AE-5124 and same has resulted in damages to the vehicle of the Petitioner.
Accordingly Issue No.1 held in the affirmative.
12. Issue No.2:
The petitioner ought to prove the expenses incurred to the repair of the car and also damages occurred in the alleged accident.

The Petitioner by producing the IMV report at Ex.P.18 has proved that his vehicle bearing No.KA-41-P- 2580 got damaged in the front bumper left side damaged, left side front fender damaged, right side front and rear door damage and right side rear body damaged.
On careful scrutiny of this document petitioner's Car was damaged to its right side Doors and the offending Cement Bulkar bearing No.KA-01 AE 5124 has got damaged to its front bumper guard left side.

It shows that the Cement Bulkar bearing No.KA-01-AE-5127 hit the Petitioner's Maruthi Alto K10 Car bearing No.KA-41-P-2580.
13.
The Petitioner has reiterated the petition averments in the evidence led as PW.1 with regard to the damages caused to his vehicle and repair cost.
The Petitioner by producing the photos and IMV report at Exs.P12 & 18 has proved that his vehicle bearing No.KA-41- P-2580 got damaged in the accident.
Apart from this, the Petitioner has also produced receipts and 3 Tax Invoices/repair bills at Ex.P.14 issued by Kalyani Motors Pvt. Ltd., for a sum of Rs.67,940/-.
This document indicates that the body of the car was totally painted, denting repair, body rubbing and polishing, upholstery cleaning and body washing.
It is the contention of the insurer that the petitioner has not got examined the author of the document to establish the expenses incurred towards repair charges.
The petitioner has produced the Counter receipt issued by the Kalyani Motor Pvt Ltd. Authorized dealer of Maruthi Suzuki.

On careful perusal of the said document marked at Ex.P13, the petitioner has spent nearly thousand rupees towards consumable items, lemen gel perfume,trim protectant,
was top kit.
Hence, an amount of Rs.1,000/- has been deducted from main bill.
When the authorized dealer has issued the bill and they have charged the amount as per the rates available on market.
Hence, it is appears to Court that non-examining of author of the document does not fatal to the case of the petitioner.
14. As discussed above the respondents have failed to prove their defense.
Therefore, the Respondents being the RC owner and Insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner.
However, as the Petitioner has proved the existence of insurance policy, the Respondent No.3 - insurer has to indemnify the Respondent No.1.
The Petitioner has claimed for a sum of Rs.5,50,000/-.

But he is entitled only for a sum of Rs.75,000/-
along with interest @ 6% per annum.
Therefore, the petition needs to be allowed.

Accordingly Issue Udaya Shankar S vs Gopi Y on 4 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/17278915/
5 No.2 is held partly in the affirmative.

sentences.text: 15. Issue No.3:-

For the reasons and discussions made above and finding to the above issues, this court proceed to pass the following:-
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner under Section 166 of Motor Vehicle Act is hereby allowed in part.
The Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.75,000/- (Rupees Seventy Five Thousand Only) along with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of depositing the amount.
The Respondents Nos.1 and 3 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner.
The Respondent No.3 insurer of the  offending vehicle shall deposit the compensation amount within sixty days from the date of this award.
On deposit of compensation and interest, entire amount shall be released in favour of the Petitioner by way of e-payment on proper identification.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw decree accordingly.
(Typed to my dictation directly on the computer by the Stenographer, corrected and then pronounced by me in open court on this the 4th day of October 2025).
